title: Period-doubling torus bundles
why: Plausible via Gueritaud layered triangulation with exponentially decaying local influence; substitutive structure should give the limit. Moderate.

title: Knotted billiards in a regular tetrahedron
why: Billiard knots known for cube (Lissajous, Jones-Przytycki) and cylinders; regular tetrahedron reflection group infinite, unfolding unavailable. Not found in literature.

title: Knotted Reeb orbits of a superball
why: H=h(x1,y1)+h(x2,y2) is separable, hence integrable; frequency ratio sweeps (0,inf), so resonant tori carry torus-knot orbits T(2,3) etc.

title: Simple closed geodesics on the Fermat quartic
why: Hard. Likely a tenth symmetric geodesic exists invariant under the order-6 rotoreflection about (1,1,1), so 'these nine are all' probably fails.

title: Outer billiards around a superellipse
why: Moser/Douady KAM boundedness needs positive curvature; flat points break twist. Analytic but degenerate case appears open.

title: Rupert superballs
why: Large p follows by perturbing the cube's strict fit; p near 2 (nearly round) is the hard part. No literature found.

title: Drum tones of superellipses
why: Faber-Krahn gives the minimum at p=2; strict monotonicity on [2,inf) for this family seems open, plausible with domain-variation estimates.

title: Chaotic billiards in a superellipse
why: Positive metric entropy for any concrete smooth convex billiard is a notorious open problem (standard-map entropy type). Extremely hard.

title: Ergodicity of the regular tetrahedron billiard
why: Ergodicity of specific polyhedral billiards is wide open even in 2D irrational polygons; essentially no tools in 3D.

title: Shifted Fujita equation
why: Shift negligible at diffusive scale sqrt(t); critical Fujita (p=2, n=2) blow-up arguments with Harnack comparisons should adapt.

title: Strauss exponent for an oscillating source
why: Oscillating cos t along light-cone characteristics yields cancellation in John iteration; threshold likely changes. Genuine open question.

title: Minimal-mass blow-up with reflection
why: Cauchy-Schwarz gives the same GN threshold; Merle-type minimal-mass classification should adapt, equality forcing symmetry about origin.

title: Heat with a cosine reaction
why: Homogenization gives effective U_t=U_xx+U^3, critical 1D Fujita; rigorous control of the oscillating term is nontrivial.

title: Difference Burgers, negative side
why: v=-u>=0 preserved; sup v nonincreasing by max principle; Holder gives d/dt||v||_p^p<=-diffusion, Nash/Moser iteration gives decay to 0.

title: Burgers with lattice viscosity
why: q=u_x obeys q'<=-q^2-2q+2 sup q0+ along characteristics (sup q bounded); steep small-oscillation data blow up, so no such c.

title: Laplacian equal to the gradient product
why: Equation scale invariant; Ladyzhenskaya-Uraltseva interior gradient bound for bounded solutions with natural growth gives |grad u(0)|<=C/R, so constant.

title: Critical NLS mass on the cube
why: Cone angle 3pi/2 threshold plausible via apex symmetrization; blow-up for every m>3/4 on compact singular surface lacks virial, hard.

title: Quintic Szegő growth
why: Unbounded Sobolev growth for a nonintegrable Hamiltonian PDE is Bourgain-type hard; H^{1/2} controlled by conservation laws only.

title: L⁴ Strichartz on a cube
why: Epsilon-loss L4 Strichartz relies on torus arithmetic; cube surface has diffractive non-arithmetic spectrum. Very hard.

title: XZ next-nearest spin chain
why: Translation plus on-site projective Z2xZ2 (X,Z) symmetry: LSM theorem (Ogata-Tasaki 2019) excludes unique gapped ground state, so gap closes.

title: Paley spin glass
why: Asks whether Boolean vectors concentrate Fourier mass on residue frequencies; well-posed, novel, numerics suggest maybe not sharp.

title: Two vortices on a cube
why: Positive entropy for a concrete 4D Hamiltonian; possible via near-collision averaging or computer-assisted horseshoe, but nontrivial.

title: Dimers on a cube surface
why: For even n the bipartite classes differ by 2 (e.g. n=2: 14 vs 12), so M_n=0 and log M_n undefined. Odd-n version is reasonable.

title: Ising spin at a cube corner
why: CFT exponent 7/24 checks (apex 1/6 plus Jacobian); discrete complex analysis on conical surfaces makes it plausible but open.

title: Kagome Hofstadter butterfly
why: Cantor spectrum proved for graphene and Lieb lattice magnetic Laplacians; kagome only has Chambers formula (Helffer et al.). Similar methods likely.

title: Spikes at the primes
why: Deterministic sparse prime barriers; random analogue gives localization, but proof needs strong pseudorandomness of primes. Very hard.

title: Fibonacci-modulated growing Jacobi matrix
why: b=0 two-step transfer matrices nearly diagonal; answer hinges on odd/even discrepancy of Fibonacci word (log growth). Tractable but open.

title: Hearing tetrahedra
why: Triangles known (Durso, Grieser-Maronna); heat invariants insufficient for tetrahedra, need wave-trace/diffractive orbits. Open.

title: Non-arithmetic tones of the cube
why: Cube is not a torus orbifold quotient (cone angle 3pi/2), so diffractive eigenvalues exist, but proving irrationality over pi^2 is hard.

title: Infinite knots in the ABC flow
why: Knotted streamlines known for some Beltrami flows (Enciso-Peralta-Salas); for the specific A=B=C=1 ABC flow needs computer-assisted horseshoe.
